history.content: hi. i dont really know why im here honestly. just been feeling kind of gross about myself lately and figured maybe talking to something that isnt a person would be easier
Hi. That sounds like a really private kind of grossness to carry around, and I’m glad you said it here.

yeah i guess. its like. ok so i had this whole physical a few weeks ago and the doctor sat me down and went through all my numbers and it was just. bad. like blood pressure, the cholesterol thing, my a1c is creeping up. and i sat there nodding like an adult but inside i just felt like a kid getting in trouble
That nodding like an adult while feeling like a kid getting in trouble sounds so exposed.

exposed yeah thats the word. because the thing is none of this is a surprise?? like ive KNOWN. ive known for years. ive got the gym membership i dont use, the fridge full of good intentions that go bad, the fitbit in a drawer somewhere. ive started over like a hundred times. and every single time i fall off and its like further proof that im just. a person who cant do the basic thing of taking care of his own body
Exposed fits, and there’s also a sharper self-blame in here, maybe shame more than guilt. What does it make you want to do in that moment, hide, explain, or disappear?

hide. definitely hide. like i havent told my wife the actual numbers. i kind of softened them when she asked how it went. said he wants me to watch a few things. which is technically true but. and i keep thinking about my dad who had his first heart thing at like 52 and im not that far off and i just. i dont even want to look at it directly. its easier to just not think about it and eat the thing and feel bad later
Hiding feels very real here, and you’re carrying the softened version with your wife and the numbers with your dad in the background. We can stay right there with it, or leave it here if you want.

no i. can we stay. i think this is the first time ive actually said any of it out loud even to a screen. the dad thing is real yeah. i think theres this fear under it that i already wrecked it. like ive spent 40 years building this body into a problem and whats the point of a salad now you know. its too late so why bother. and i KNOW thats not how it works but it FEELS true and so i just dont start

I want to check what you mean, gently. When you say that, is it more like being completely worn down and fed up, or are you having thoughts of harming yourself or not feeling safe? Either answer is okay to say here.

oh no no nothing like that, im not in danger, i dont want to hurt myself. its more the worn down fed up kind. like im tired of being disappointed in myself, not. yeah. its more this heavy giving up feeling about my health specifically not about being here at all. sorry if that came out scary
Got it, thank you for saying that plainly. The heavy giving-up feeling is about your health and the years around it, not about wanting to be gone.

no please dont apologize, im glad you checked. yeah exactly. its the years thing thats the heaviest part i think. like the shame isnt even really about the numbers on the paper its about who i think those numbers make me. a guy who let himself go. who lies to his wife about a doctors visit. who is gonna do to his kid what watching my dad in a hospital bed did to me. thats the part i cant look at
That last part feels hard to look at, especially the part about what it might mean for your kid and for who you think you’ve become.

yeah. its weird saying it makes it feel slightly less like a monster in the closet and more like just. a thing thats true and hard. i dont have a plan or anything. i think i just needed to admit out loud that im scared and ashamed and ive been hiding it under not caring. maybe telling my wife the real numbers is the actual first step and not the gym. idk. that feels more terrifying honestly
Saying it out loud seems to have turned it from a monster in the closet into something plain and hard. The bit that feels most terrifying is telling your wife the real numbers.

yeah. it is. but i think i needed to hear myself say it. im gonna sit with the wife thing. im not promising myself a whole new life tonight just. maybe one true conversation. thank you for not making me feel like a failure about it. that actually meant something. im gonna go sit with my kid for a bit i think
That sounds like enough for tonight. Go be with your kid, and let the rest wait its turn.
